title: Morning Intel
bullets: Markets: Bitcoin rallied to about $81,250 Saturday (+~4%) with altcoins outperforming - ETH +5.3%, XRP +6.1%, SOL and HYPE both +10%+ - as the Fear & Greed Index climbed to 71 ("Greed") on strong spot-ETF inflows.
Markets: Crude oil holds near $99-100/bbl, still up a third straight week on Middle East supply risk, after easing off Tuesday's four-month high near $106.
Markets: Berkshire Hathaway's B shares extended Friday's slide as investors keep digesting Warren Buffett's move to chairman emeritus, with son Howard now chair and Greg Abel remaining CEO.
Companies: Coinbase Derivatives, Kalshi and Bitnomial are all racing to launch single-stock perpetual futures, deepening the crypto/TradFi crossover.
Companies: Deutsche Bank plans to offer Bitcoin and digital-asset custody to European institutional clients by the end of 2026.
Companies: Week-ahead earnings to watch - Costco, AutoZone and Lennar all report Tuesday, Sept. 22.

Macro/Policy: The Fed's 25bp hike to 3.75%-4.00% (first since 2023) and the Bank of Japan's hike to 1.25% (highest since 1995, on a split 7-2 vote that oddly weakened the yen past 157/dollar) remain the dominant policy backdrop.

Macro/Policy: Markets are focused on the Sept. 24 Trump-Xi summit in Washington - Xi's first U.S. state visit in over a decade - expecting a tactical extension of the trade truce (the rare-earths truce expires Nov. 10) rather than a grand bargain; the Bank of England also sets rates this week.
